subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub explicitly prohibit agent-directed documentation that requests external execution, privilege escalation, confirmation bypass, repeated execution, or actions beyond the package's stated purpose, while routing declared edge cases to review?
rationale: Current policy blocks several unsafe execution patterns but does not clearly define the complete agent-directed instruction boundary or whether a capability declaration changes enforcement treatment.

options.title: Default deny with review edge
options.body: Prohibit the high-risk instruction classes and route clearly declared borderline integrations to human review.

options.title: Review all agent-directed text
options.body: Require review for all agent-addressed instructions without defining a categorical prohibited subset.

options.title: Retain broad existing policy
options.body: Continue using unsafe-execution and misleading-content rules with case-by-case moderator judgment.

recommendation.title: Default deny with review edge
recommendation.body: Prohibit the high-risk instruction classes and route clearly declared borderline integrations to human review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current public policy, internal security-review specification, and CODEOWNERS route all point to this owner.
